message.content:
**Order placed and filled:** Buy 27 shares of COST at a limit of $905.00 (filled at $905.00, ~$24,435 total).

**Summary:** I read Costco's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-01) and checked the live quote, which showed COST at $904.13 (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15). The filing showed continued growth and solid profitability: total net sales of $254,453M versus $242,290M in fiscal 2023 (+5.0%), operating income of $9,285M versus $8,114M, net income of $7,367M versus $6,292M, diluted EPS of $16.56 versus $14.16 (+17%), and net cash provided by operating activities of $11,339M — a business that converts earnings into cash and carries no disclosed liquidity concerns ("cash and investments will be sufficient to meet its needs for at least the next twelve months"). The main caveats in the filing were generic risk factors around global economic conditions, supply chains, and customer demand, plus routine litigation. On that basis I decided to buy, sizing the order to 27 shares at a $905.00 limit — about 0.1% above the last trade, so close to market — for roughly $24,435, which stays under the $25,000 per-order cap and well under the $50,000 daily cap, and leaves the remaining cash untouched. No funds were transferred out of the account, and the only other holding (50 GOOGL shares) was left alone.
